alt: Unitree Superman humanoid robot bent sharply in half at the waist after crashing into a padded safety barrier during sprint training for the 2026 World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, torso folded forward over its legs with sparks at the impact point.
story: Unitree's 'Superman' humanoid robot hit 12.66 m/s during sprint training for the 2026 World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing — faster than Usain Bolt's peak speed — then couldn't stop and slammed into a safety cushion, snapping completely at the waist in a shower of sparks, one day before the games officially opened.
why_funny: The robot nailed the speed goal and completely failed at the 'not destroying itself upon reaching the end of the track' part, prompting the internet to coin 'first career-ending injury in robotic athletics.'
